feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by concrete platform, analytics, and content achievements. It is clear and well-written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with some formatting inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support leadership in digital platforms, governance, and communications systems.  
- Good credibility and impact: examples like a 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, and building an in-house studio add substance.  
- Broad but coherent skill set: strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are aligned and relevant.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition: “digital strategy,” “governance,” “workflows,” and “communications operations” recur across sections; tighten to make each role feel more distinct.  
- Improve structure: the “Recent Projects” content in the footer is valuable but oddly placed; move it into a dedicated Projects section. Also consolidate overlapping skills sections (“Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT”).  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak filler; title casing is inconsistent (“Coleman DAVIS” vs standard capitalization). No major misspellings or serious grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly broad and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and foreground the strongest differentiators: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and public-sector scale.
- Add 1–2 concrete signals of scope from recent roles (for example, large public-facing platforms or multi-publisher environments) without overloading the intro.
- Replace “Leads” with a parallel construction tied to value delivered, e.g., “Specializes in” or “Drives,” for smoother style.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance models and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Drives digital strategy across website transformation, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled content discovery for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled content discovery” is more specific and less repetitive.
- “Digital leader” in the intro and “Leader” in the subtitle may feel slightly repetitive.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities will make it feel more distinct and executive-level.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and shorten longer items for cleaner scanning.
- Replace “Multi-channel communications operations” with “Multi-channel communications leadership” to better match seniority.
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve more tactical terms like “livestream operations” or “editorial systems” for skills/technical sections and keep this block strategic.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” are already strongly covered in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” closely overlaps with the header’s “public-sector communications” and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots that reinforce your current positioning, but they read a bit dense and overlap with achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope where possible would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, punchier structure: “Project name: action + platform/format + purpose/outcome.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “designed for continued campaign growth” with a sharper benefit, e.g., “built for reuse and future campaign expansion.”
- Standardize style and hyphenation: “AI-enabled,” “bill-level,” “10-by-20-foot,” and consider “social media” instead of just “social.”
- Consider this tighter wording: “Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level chat to improve policy discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially repeat current NACo bullets; keep this section more selective or frame these as standout examples not fully captured above.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item here and adds the most new information.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the prior NACo positions and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, strategic outcomes, and only the newest/highest-value contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise web strategy, digital governance, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery as an external consultant.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-focused lines; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet on improving cross-channel communications operations.
- Emphasize consultant-specific impact: strategy, architecture, governance, and delivery oversight; reduce lower-level phrasing like “technical troubleshooting.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/campaigns launched, toolkit downloads, search improvement metrics, publishing efficiency gains, or stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal microsites,” “analytics,” “governance,” and “AI-enabled search” are already echoed in the footer projects and earlier NACo roles; avoid repeating implementation detail here.
- CMS/front-end execution may undersell this recent role if the prior Director role already establishes hands-on platform leadership.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were less list-like and if channel oversight emphasized outcomes, team leadership, and enterprise change rather than broad responsibilities.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the first sentence with a tighter leadership summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management for a national membership organization.”
- Recast bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel impact more specific if possible: add email open/click growth, audience growth, engagement rates, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements.
- Combine operations/governance bullets into one concise enterprise-systems point: “Built analytics and publishing infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery while formalizing governance, standards, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video-program growth overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on building the in-house studio and scaling capacity.
- Governance/editorial coordination also appears in adjacent NACo roles; emphasize enterprise ownership here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed at this level: ownership of day-to-day operations, newsletter scale, and launch/growth of recurring advocacy video.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-value points: managed four weekly newsletters; produced/scaled weekly advocacy video update; coordinated editorial planning across communications/advocacy/program teams; improved publishing workflows.
- Add metrics where possible: open/click rates, video views, production cadence, turnaround time, stakeholder groups served, or workflow efficiency gains.
- Use stronger verbs: “managed,” “launched,” “scaled,” “standardized,” “coordinated,” “streamlined” instead of “helped.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager role and footer project; frame this here as scaling/operationalizing, not originating.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with Director of Digital Media; keep this version tactical and execution-focused.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

Suggested edit:

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to outcomes + decision support, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets if formatting allows.
- Replace generic phrases with stronger business language: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive dashboarding and leadership reporting” instead of “Leadership reporting.”
- Add one optimization concept already supported by experience, such as: “SEO, UX insight and performance analysis.”

Possible rewrite:
- Analytics strategy and reporting infrastructure
- GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity
- KPI framework development and executive dashboarding
- SEO, UX insight and performance optimization

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Livestreaming

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and operational scope rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership + delivery: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”

- If space allows, align wording with proven experience: “in-house studio buildout” or “advocacy programming and event production.”

- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrase verbatim.
- This section should not restate older hands-on editing work if recent roles emphasize leading studio, video, and event capability.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either add level/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Web Platforms & CMS Administration
- Rewrite as: Drupal (primary; enterprise/public-sector sites, migrations, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Put Drupal first and add “primary” or brief scope, since recent roles and projects clearly center on Drupal and enterprise web modernization.
- Standardize naming: use “Microsoft Power Pages” instead of “Power Pages” for clarity and ATS matching.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“Web Platforms & Technical Execution”), which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- If space is tight, keep the stronger Topline Skills section and use this item only if you add differentiators like primary platform, migration/admin scope, or enterprise context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior, recent-profile CV, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to applied capability: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used consistently elsewhere; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation.”
- Order by relevance/modernity: JavaScript • API integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • Google Tag Manager • HTML/CSS • jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Analytics/Optimization if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. Since the CV already emphasizes workflow architecture elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more clearly framed around automation and operational coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools”
- Reorder by relevance to the rest of the CV: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Microsoft Teams • Slack • Trello • Basecamp”
- If accurate, add light functional grouping for clarity: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team coordination: Teams, Slack”
- If these tools were used to build systems, consider replacing 1–2 names with capability phrasing: “Airtable-based workflow systems • Power Automate and Zapier automations • Jira/Asana project operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same wording verbatim.
- Slack/Teams overlap with general workplace tools; keep them only if they were central to workflow design.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the operational/email leadership context shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal platform administration and campaign execution without repeating broader “multi-channel communications” claims.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more specific: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Expand from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp — email campaign operations, newsletter publishing, audience segmentation, and engagement workflows**
- If accurate, add scale or ownership language tied to recent work: **enterprise/member communications**, **newsletter distribution**, or **journey/campaign setup**
- Keep only the strongest/current platforms; list in order of recency/relevance, likely **Dynamics 365, Higher Logic, Mailchimp**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating audience scale here (“tens of thousands”) since that already appears in Work Experience.
- “Engagement” may overlap with Core Competencies; use this line to emphasize systems/platforms, not strategy.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the Director role. Make it more execution-focused and trim broad terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • KPI design • SEO/performance analysis • Experimentation**
- Replace vague nouns like **Dashboarding** with stronger capability language such as **KPI design**, **reporting**, or **performance analysis**.
- Consider changing **A/B testing** to **Experimentation** only if you can support it with examples/results elsewhere; otherwise keep **A/B testing**.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recent tools first: **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider merging or differentiating one as strategic outcomes and the other as tools only.
- Avoid repeating the exact same analytics stack already named in the 2022–2024 Director role unless this section is strictly a keyword/tool index.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer outcomes if you can add metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving execution across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “coordinated daily work with a digital media associate.”
- If available, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social engagement, or workflow efficiencies.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” and “weekly video updates” overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on helping launch the team and executing content.
- Avoid repeating website/email/social oversight language already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the policy/research support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research coordination and program content development.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output: number of episodes, audiences served, cross-team partners, or types of multimedia assets produced.
- Consider a stronger full version: “Coordinated research and innovation projects supporting NACo’s program and policy teams. Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching the organization’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research coordination + first podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating leadership in digital operations here, since that growth is already shown in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
